preferences.heading: Language & region
preferences.description: Choose the language, time zone, and theme color used across UniMailbox.
preferences.timeZoneDescription: Message and administration timestamps use this time zone.
preferences.themeColorDescription: The interface derives accessible accents and highlights from this color.

account.heading: Login identity
account.description: This email is only your UniMailbox login. It does not create, select, or modify a mailbox or sending domain.
account.warning: Email or password changes revoke every refresh session. You will sign in again with the updated credentials.

cloudflare.accountDescription: OAuth is optional. Dashboard-assisted mode only records your account and zone IDs, then gives you exact links for Email Routing and DNS.
cloudflare.domainDescription: Add the domain that receives mail. With OAuth, UniMailbox verifies the zone and prepares its Email Routing catch-all.
cloudflare.manualRoutingIntro: <name>{{name}}</name> was added to UniMailbox, but Cloudflare Email Routing has not been configured yet.
cloudflare.manualRoutingOnboard: Select Onboard Domain in Email Routing, then choose <name>{{name}}</name>.
cloudflare.manualRoutingDns: Allow Cloudflare to add the required MX, SPF, and DKIM records.
cloudflare.manualRoutingCatchAll: Create or enable the catch-all rule and choose Send to a Worker → <worker>unimailbox</worker>.
cloudflare.manualRoutingReturn: Return here and run the inbound smoke test after Cloudflare shows the routing records as configured.
cloudflare.inboundDescription: Generate a one-time subject, send it to the displayed address, then verify that the Worker accepted the message.
cloudflare.subject: Subject
cloudflare.providerDescription: API credentials are encrypted before storage. The login email is never used as a sender or mailbox address.
cloudflare.deliveryDescription: Send one operational test message before using the provider for normal mailbox traffic.

storage.requiredDescription: D1, KV, Queue, and Assets are provisioned with the deployment. Mail storage remains operational on KV when no R2 binding is present.
storage.instructions: Add an ATTACHMENTS R2 binding in Cloudflare, deploy with wrangler.r2.jsonc, then return here to verify. Existing KV objects remain readable during migration.
storage.verified: R2 write, head, and cleanup probe passed.

mcp.heading: Model context tokens
mcp.description: Issue scoped, long-lived credentials for external AI agents that connect to the first-party MCP server. Each token inherits a subset of your permissions and can be revoked at any time.
mcp.listEmpty: You have not issued any agent tokens yet.
mcp.confirmRevoke: Revoke this token? It will stop working immediately and cannot be undone.
mcp.plaintextWarning: This is the only time the plaintext token is shown. Store it in a secret manager before navigating away. If you lose it, issue a new token.
